newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO crawl forward on Hebron but no deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO crawl forward on Hebron but no deal.

text.p: Israelis and Palestinians reported progress on Wednesday in talks on a delayed troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron but wide gaps remained.
Officials said the talks were snagged on Israel's demand that its soldiers be allowed to enter Hebron "in hot pursuit" of suspected attackers.
PLO officials said they did not expect agreement before Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu left for the United States on Wednesday night.
Negotiators returned to the table on Wednesday after saying U.S.-brokered talks overnight between Palestinian Mahmoud Abbas and Israeli army chief Lieutenant-General Amnon Shahak were "positive".

"We have held talks in a positive atmosphere. We exchanged ideas and there was a desire from both sides to reach an agreement," chief negotiator Abbas told Reuters. "We have not reached an agreement yet. The talks will continue."
Israeli government spokesman Moshe Fogel said progress had been "significant".

"They are actually trying to formulate in writing the bounds and limits and ways the Israeli military will be allowed to act in areas of control of the Palestinian Authority," Fogel told reporters in Hebron.
Fogel said Israel sought to define how it could act in Palestinian-run areas against "terrorists".
But Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat denied there was any such discussion.
"We have not reached agreement because Israel is still insisting on hot pursuit. They want the right to enter areas under Palestinian control and this has been rejected by us," Erekat told Reuters.
"We will not change our position that there be no change in the agreement," he said.
Fogel said Netanyahu might delay his U.S. trip if an agreement was at hand. "As of now, he is going to the United States but I think there will be a re-examiniation of this this afternoon."
Netanyahu wants the Hebron deal signed by Israel's previous government modified to safeguard the 400 Jewish settlers who live in guarded enclaves among 100,000 Arabs.
The Hebron pullout was due last March but was delayed after Islamist suicide bomb attacks in Israel.
